title: Strict preferred-window robustness is unreachable in the frozen candidate set
quantitative_support: 0/117 nominal-feasible candidates contain their full actual uncertainty intervals inside all three preferred windows.
claim: The strict robustness target is unreachable under the current uncertainty definition; a robust winner should not be assigned under this gate.
limitations: Synthetic benchmark intervals; not experimental uncertainty.

title: The compounded viscosity-ratio interval is the dominant robustness bottleneck
quantitative_support: WO_INV_0420 requires uncertainty scale <= 0.587 (about 41.3% reduction); limiting coordinate = ratio.
claim: Robustness failure is driven primarily by thermal-sensitivity/ratio uncertainty rather than nominal eta80 or eta120 location.
limitations: Depends on frozen interval construction including compounded ratio bounds.

title: Backward robustness quantifies how far the target is from reachability
quantitative_support: Best candidate by window relaxation is WO_INV_0359, requiring preferred half-width expansion factor 1.486; best uniform uncertainty-shrink solution is WO_INV_0374, requiring at least 34.4% reduction.
claim: The robustness layer can return a quantitative reachability gap instead of inventing a winner when no candidate passes.
limitations: Gap is defined relative to the current preferred windows and synthetic interval model.
